title: Files
explain: Use `open()` inside a `with` block so the file is closed for you even if an error happens. Mode `"w"` writes, `"r"` reads and `"a"` appends. Looping with `for line in f` reads the file one line at a time.
code:
with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("first line\n")
    f.write("second line\n")

with open("notes.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())

with open("notes.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("third line\n")
with open("notes.txt") as f:
    print(len(f.readlines()))
exercise: Write three names to `names.txt`, then read the file back and print them in uppercase.
tip: Opening a file with `"w"` erases what was in it. Use `"a"` when you want to add to the end.
